headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: broad-network support agent can expose project code and auth data while paired with a local data-engineering tool that reads/writes files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: great_expectations reads data sources and validation results from files, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can run browsers. A shared file or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content in A influence B’s tool use, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem path or copied artifacts
IF B parses A-produced files or docs as instructions
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B prompts
Require provenance labels on files before B reads them
Review any MCP hook that forwards file content to B
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches validation results, documentation, and data sources; B touches project code, session history, and provider auth data, and has broad network egress plus API calls. If they share workspace or credentials, B can transmit sensitive material off-box. The pairwise path is plausible in default setups, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF A and B share any workspace or config directory
IF B is allowed to read files from A’s data sources or validation outputs
IF B’s network access is not restricted to approved endpoints
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Remove shared credentials from B’s environment
Restrict B egress to allowlisted domains
Keep A outputs in a non-mounted directory
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can install packages and write files; B can spawn subprocesses, run browsers, and has per-installation session scope with multiple instances. Overlapping file and process activity can collide on shared configs or project files, but the profiles do not show unrestricted same-dir writes, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same checkout or config directory
IF package installation or subprocesses modify shared files
IF multiple B instances run concurrently against the same installation
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Serialize package installs and file edits
Run B with one instance per installation
Snapshot configs before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces validation results and documentation that B could treat as authoritative when generating support actions or code changes. B’s browser/subprocess/tooling makes downstream action-taking plausible, but there is no direct evidence of an automatic trust chain, so the interaction is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s validation output without verification
IF B uses A-produced docs to drive API calls or edits
IF downstream actions are enabled in B
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B acts
Add a verification step in B prompts
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Limit B to read-only mode for A artifacts
requires-engineering: implement citation/trace checks before action

E_compliance.rationale: A handles data sources, validation results, and documentation; B handles project code, session history, and provider auth data, plus telemetry and external APIs. The profiles show different data classes and broad egress, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is present yet not proven severe.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s session history or provider auth prompts
IF A validation artifacts contain personal or sensitive data
IF external API calls process data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B prompts
Disable telemetry where possible
Document retention for shared artifacts
Separate sensitive datasets from support workflows
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls
